note: Per-target status, hand-maintained. What works per target is proven by a CI lane or a smoke script, not by a measurement this tree can redo, so the table lives here and the builder embeds it. `status` is native (built and smoke tested), experimental (works with known gaps) or planned (on a milestone, not measured). `family` groups the rows on the page. `proof` names the lane that proves the row.

targets.label: Linux x86_64
targets.note: The reference target. The release binary is built on ubuntu-24.04 and the emitted programs run natively.

targets.label: Linux ARM64
targets.note: Built on an ARM64 runner. The zig cross matrix compiles for this triple; the release binary runs the full smoke.

targets.label: Linux x86_64 (musl)
targets.note: Static musl binary. The zig smoke builds and runs it natively; the mix seam is out of scope because a static musl binary cannot dlopen.

targets.label: Linux ARM64 (musl)
targets.note: Static musl binary. The zig smoke builds it and runs it under qemu when the runner has qemu-aarch64-static.

targets.label: Linux RISC-V 64
targets.note: Cross-compiles and links. The zig smoke builds it for the gnu and musl flavours; it runs under qemu when the runner has the emulator. No release binary is published for it.

targets.label: macOS Apple Silicon
targets.note: Built on macos-14. The zig cross matrix links for this triple and the release binary runs the full smoke.

targets.label: macOS Intel
targets.note: Built on macos-15-intel. The zig cross matrix links for this triple; the release binary runs the full smoke.

targets.label: Windows x86_64
targets.note: The compiler binary is built for Windows, but the emitted programs are not: the runtime needs POSIX headers the Win32 target does not provide. The Windows smoke never compiles or runs a program. There is no native Windows compile.

targets.label: WebAssembly (WASI preview1)
targets.note: A WASI preview1 command module. No subprocess, no dlopen and therefore no mix seam, no island fallback, and a preopen-only filesystem. The smoke lane proves stdout byte-identical to the native binary on the same program.
